topics.label: Lecture introduction and the cancer hallmarks framework
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s learning outcomes and introduces the hallmarks framework for understanding loss of growth control.

topics.label: Mutated signaling pathways promote growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted cellular maturation contributes to cancer and can be recognized in the affected tissue.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells evade mitochondrial apoptosis by disabling p53 activity or altering the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how increased telomerase expression allows cancer cells to bypass it.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of mutation-driven loss of growth control by explaining normal protective responses and reviewing the hallmarks already discussed.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism characterizes cancer cells and participates in self-reinforcing changes to their regulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis supports tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why tumor expansion depends on an angiogenic switch that supplies oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Metastatic spread, survival and genetic signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what enables cancer cells to leave a primary tumor and establish detectable tumors at distant sites.

topics.label: Concluding summary and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture’s central message about shared hallmarks, recommends further reading and invites questions.
